payload.description_html:
Fossil Plioplatecarpus skull at the Charles M. Russell National Wildlife Refuge in Phillips County, Montana. At the Museum of the Rockies in Bozeman, Montana. Mosasaurs are not dinosaurs, but lizards.

These animals lived about 70 to 65 million years ago, and were about 60 feet long. They looked like a crocodile with flippers, and hunted fish, reptiles, and other dinosaurs in the Inland Seaway -- a vast shallow ocean that occupied central North America from the Rocky Mountains to the Appalachians (all the way from the Gulf of Mexico north to the Arctic Sea).
